primitives.name: Ordinary Least Squares linear regression (minimum sum of squared residuals)
primitives.verbatim_quote: Technically, OLS regression finds the coefficients that make the total sum of each squared residual as small as possible.
primitives.latex: y = b_0 + b_1 x_1 + b_2 x_2 + \cdots + b_n x_n, \qquad \min_{b}\ \sum_{j}\big(y_j - \hat{y}_j\big)^2
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Source notation (printed p.177/181, PDF p.187/191) is ASCII: 'y = b0 + b1*x1 + b2*x2 + ... + ... bn*xn' and the objective in footnote 4. y = output variable [unit depends on target: dimensionless probability in the TD model, or fantasy points]; x_i = input column i [feature unit, e.g. yards to endzone]; b_i = slope coefficient on x_i [y-unit per x_i-unit]; b_0 = intercept [y-unit]; n = number of inputs [count]; j indexes observations [count]; \hat{y}_j = fitted value [y-unit]; residual y_j-\hat{y}_j [y-unit]; squared residual [(y-unit)^2]. Each term b_i x_i carries y-unit, so the sum is dimensionally homogeneous; the objective minimizes a sum of squared residuals (squares keep it positive so the model cannot 'minimize' by underpredicting everything negative, per the source footnote).
primitives.assumptions: Printed equations exist (PDF p.187 linear form, p.191 objective footnote). Stated: OLS = Ordinary Least Squares = basic standard linear regression; the computer picks b0,b1,b2 to make residuals as small as possible, technically the total sum of each squared residual. Implicit Gauss-Markov-style assumptions the book does not state: linear-in-parameters specification, exogenous inputs, homoskedastic non-autocorrelated errors for inference. The book's own TD fit reports Condition No. 11073 and warns of strong multicollinearity, and R^2 of only 0.090 on 292 observations from two games.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks under multicollinearity (the book's condition number 1e4 flag; perfectly correlated inputs like td and not_a_td break the model and get auto-dropped, footnote 3); under nonlinearity (a linear probability model returns negative probabilities mid-field, which motivates the logistic primitive p2); under tiny samples (two games, 292 plays) so coefficients are noisy; and when inputs are endogenous. R^2 in [0,1] measures explained variation, not causal truth.
timescales: tau_fit ~ one batch solve on n observations
tau_refit ~ weekly as new data arrives

layer2.mapping: Binds to the GSE projection / value kernel: a linear-in-parameters predictor of player fantasy points or play outcome from feature columns, fit by minimizing squared residuals. In the Coach-Mind sim this is the baseline value function before nonlinear links; the design matrix X and coefficient vector b are the learned transition from observable features to expected output, and the residual sum of squares is the calibration loss.
layer2.telemetry: Design matrix X, coefficient vector b, residual sum of squares, R^2 and adjusted R^2, condition number (multicollinearity flag), and per-coefficient standard errors. Causal identification is LATENT_UNIDENTIFIABLE from a predictive OLS fit alone (needs the holding-constant structure of p3).

primitives.name: Logistic (logit) link bounding a linear predictor to a probability
primitives.verbatim_quote: but for some yardlines around the middle of the field it returned negative probabilities. We can avoid this by running a logistic regression instead of OLS.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Source notation (printed p.192, PDF p.202) is ASCII: 'Logit: 1/(1 + exp(-(b0 + b1*x1 + ... + bn*xn)))' vs OLS 'b0 + b1*x1 + ... + bn*xn'. z = b_0 + b_1 x_1 + ... + b_n x_n = linear predictor [dimensionless log-odds]; exp(z) [dimensionless]; \hat{p} = output probability [dimensionless, strictly in (0,1)]; b_i [log-odds per x_i-unit]; x_i [feature unit, e.g. yards to endzone]; b_0 [log-odds]. The argument of exp must be dimensionless, which forces z to be dimensionless log-odds; the sigmoid maps the real line to (0,1), so the output is a valid probability for every input. Dimensionally homogeneous and bounded by construction.
primitives.assumptions: Printed equation exists (PDF p.202). Stated motivation: the OLS probability-of-touchdown model returned negative probabilities for mid-field yardlines, so a logistic regression is used instead; all the same right-hand-side tricks (interactions, fixed effects, squared, dummy, logged variables) still apply. Implicit: the log-odds are linear in the inputs; the link is the canonical logistic. The book does not print the likelihood or fitting algorithm.
primitives.breakdown_regime: The link guarantees (0,1) but does not guarantee calibration: a misspecified linear log-odds still yields overconfident or biased probabilities; separation (a feature perfectly predicting TD) drives coefficients to infinity; extrapolation far outside the training yardline range saturates near 0 or 1 with false certainty. The fix removes the negative-probability symptom of p1, not the underlying specification error.

layer2.mapping: Binds to the bounded play-outcome probability kernel of the Coach-Mind sim: touchdown probability, completion probability, and win probability must live in [0,1], so the logistic link is the admissible output map for any linear predictor of a binary football event. It is the probability-consistent replacement for the linear probability model whenever the output is a chance rather than a continuous quantity.
layer2.telemetry: Predicted probabilities \hat{p} in (0,1), log-loss, Brier score, calibration curve (reliability diagram), and the OLS negative-probability rate that triggered the switch. True event probability is LATENT_UNIDENTIFIABLE per single play; only repeated calibration identifies it.

primitives.name: Ceteris-paribus coefficient interpretation / omitted-variable control
primitives.verbatim_quote: Now that yards is explicitly accounted for, we know that the first_down coefficient measures only the effect of new set of downs.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Source notation (printed p.185-187, PDF p.195-197) is the statsmodels formula 'wpa ~ offensive_td + turnover + first_down + yards_gained'. wpa = win probability added [dimensionless probability delta]; offensive_td, turnover, first_down = dummy variables [dimensionless 0/1]; yards_gained [yards]; b_0 intercept [probability delta]; b_1,b_2,b_3 [probability delta per dummy unit]; b_4 [probability delta per yard]. Every term carries probability-delta unit, so the sum is homogeneous. The coefficient b_3 is the partial effect of a new set of downs holding TD, turnover, and yards gained constant; the source reports b_3 falling from 0.0573 (without yards) to 0.0224 (with yards), the omitted-variable bias made visible.
primitives.assumptions: Printed model and coefficient tables exist (PDF p.196-197). Stated principle: the interpretation of a coefficient assumes all other variables in the model are held constant; adding yards_gained isolates the new-set-of-downs effect from the extra yards first-down plays gain. Implicit: the control set is sufficient to block the confounding path (no unmeasured common cause of first_down and wpa); the book explicitly notes win probability itself is modeled and 'taken as given'.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks when a confounder is omitted (the first_down coefficient is biased upward until yards is controlled); when controls are themselves outcomes or colliders (conditioning on a post-treatment variable induces bias); when 'held constant' is extrapolation beyond the data's support; and when the taken-as-given wpa model is itself wrong, propagating error into every coefficient. Holding constant is a statement about the model, not a guarantee of causal identification.

layer2.mapping: Binds to the conditioning / confounding-control operator of the 22-player dynamical system: a regression coefficient is the partial effect of one state variable on an outcome with the rest of the state held fixed, exactly the operation needed to disentangle play-type effects (first down vs yards gained) in the Coach-Mind sim. Omitted-variable bias is the failure mode when a latent defensive-state variable is left out of the conditioning set.
layer2.telemetry: Coefficient vector with and without each control, the first_down shift 0.0573 -> 0.0224 when yards_gained enters, partial R^2, and the conditioning set used. The true causal partial effect is LATENT_UNIDENTIFIABLE unless the control set blocks all back-door paths (untestable from the fit alone).

primitives.name: P-value as null-survival frequency and the replicability crisis (p-hacking veto)
primitives.verbatim_quote: But if you keep running regressions until you find something you like, the traditional interpretation of a P value goes out the window.
primitives.assumptions: Prose epistemic primitive (printed p.182-184, PDF p.192-194); no equation is printed for the p-value, so latex is null rather than fabricated. Stated definition: significance asks whether an observed effect is real or luck of the draw, by (1) assuming the true effect is none, then (2) asking how often data this extreme would appear under that assumption; the coin-flip example separates the true relationship (calling heads cannot affect a fair toss) from the noisy observed relationship. Traditional threshold P<0.05; the book documents that 100 researchers testing null effects yield ~5 false 'significant' results, that one analyst can run many specifications until something looks significant, and that this drives the replicability crisis; remedies are pre-registration and stricter thresholds.
primitives.breakdown_regime: The P<0.05 interpretation collapses under multiple comparisons and specification search (p-hacking): the nominal false-positive rate no longer holds once many models are tried; publication bias selects the lucky five; a 'significant' effect fails to replicate on new data. A statistically insignificant effect may still be interesting (the book insists on this). The p-value is not the probability the null is true, and significance is not effect size or causal truth.
timescales: tau_field ~ years of published false positives

layer2.mapping: Binds to the falsifier / multiple-comparisons discipline of the GSE edge-hunt: a p-value is the survival frequency of an observed edge under the null of no edge, and pre-registration is the held-out protocol that prevents scoring a fit on its own search rows. The replicability crisis is the corpus-level warning that an edge found by trying many specifications is noise wearing a significance badge, exactly the held-out discipline the Foundry crucible enforces.
layer2.telemetry: Number of specifications tried, family-wise error / false-discovery rate, pre-registered hypothesis vs explored ones, and out-of-sample replication rate of each claimed edge. Whether any single 'significant' edge is real is LATENT_UNIDENTIFIABLE without an independent hold-out.

primitives.name: Quadratic marginal effect via the power rule (state-dependent derivative)
primitives.verbatim_quote: Including squared (sometimes called quadratic) variables is common when you think the relationship between an input and output might depend where you are on the input.
primitives.latex: \frac{d}{dx}\big(b_0 + b_1 x + b_2 x^2\big) = b_1 + 2 b_2 x
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Source notation (printed p.189-190, PDF p.199-200) is ASCII: 'ave points = b0 + b1*adp + b2*adp^2' and the marginal effect 'b1 + 2*b2*(ADP we're at currently)'. x = ADP / average draft position [draft pick position, count]; b_0 [fantasy points]; b_1 [points per pick]; b_2 [points per pick^2]; the derivative d(ave points)/dx [points per pick]. b_2 x^2 carries points, so the quadratic is homogeneous; its derivative b_1 + 2 b_2 x carries points per pick, matching b_1. The marginal effect of ADP on points depends on the current pick x, unlike the constant b_1 of the purely linear model; the source notes early-ADP differences matter more than late-ADP differences.
primitives.assumptions: Printed equation and power-rule derivative exist (PDF p.200, with calculus footnote 5). Stated: squaring ADP keeps the model linear in parameters while letting the effect vary with position on the input; the derivative is b1 + 2*b2*(current ADP). Implicit: the quadratic is an adequate local approximation of the true ADP->points curve; the book motivates it by the intuition that early picks matter more, not by a fitted curvature test.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks when the true relationship is not well approximated by a quadratic over the range (a single turning point may be spurious); extrapolation beyond the observed ADP range makes the x^2 term dominate and can flip the sign of the marginal effect unrealistically; b_2 estimated on few early picks is noisy. The derivative is a local statement, valid only near the data's support.
timescales: tau_eval ~ marginal effect at a given pick

layer2.mapping: Binds to the state-dependent marginal-value kernel of the GSE DFS/portfolio value function: the marginal value of an input (draft position, usage, target share) is not constant but varies with the current state, captured by the derivative b_1 + 2 b_2 x. This is the nonlinear value-function correction that a purely linear projection misses, and it is the calculus behind diminishing or accelerating returns across the input range.
layer2.telemetry: Coefficient b_2 (curvature), the marginal-effect curve b_1 + 2 b_2 x across the input range, the turning point -b_1/(2 b_2) if in range, and held-out error of quadratic vs linear. The true functional form is LATENT_UNIDENTIFIABLE from a single quadratic fit.

primitives.name: Composite scores by weighting plus percentile rescaling (SPARQ / passer-rating pattern)
primitives.verbatim_quote: Most of these composite scores make use of two statistical concepts: weighting and rescaling.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: DERIVED FORMALIZATION of prose (printed p.171, PDF p.181): the source states composites use 'weighting and rescaling' and that raw components are converted to percentiles before combining; it prints no formula, so the LaTeX is the standard dimensionally-homogeneous formalization, labelled as derived. p_i = percentile-rescaled component i [dimensionless percentile, 0-100 or 0-1]; w_i = weight on component i [dimensionless, probability simplex, sum=1, w_i>=0]; k = number of components [count]; C = composite score [same percentile unit as p_i]. Rescaling to percentiles makes heterogeneous raw units (40-yard dash seconds, shuttle seconds, vertical-jump inches) commensurable before the weighted sum; the sum is homogeneous because every p_i shares the percentile unit.
primitives.assumptions: Prose primitive (PDF p.181). Stated: composite scores (passer rating on a 0-158.3 scale, SPARQ = speed/power/agility/reaction/quickness) use weighting and rescaling; raw values are converted to percentiles relative to a peer group (e.g. a 4.6 forty for a 6'5" 260-lb rusher at the 98th percentile) before combining. The author explicitly distrusts composites because their calculation is opaque ('do you know how to calculate QBR?') and prefers multiple columns of real data.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks under opacity (unpublished weights/normalizations make the composite unauditable, the author's QBR critique); under peer-group dependence (a percentile is relative to a chosen reference population, so the same raw value rescales differently across groups); under loss of cardinal information (percentiles discard magnitude and tail shape); and under arbitrary weights that encode the builder's priorities rather than a validated relationship to the outcome.
timescales: tau_measure ~ combine event (40 dash, shuttle, vertical)
tau_recompute ~ when peer group or weights change

layer2.mapping: Binds to the GSI/GSE composite-index fusion kernel: heterogeneous telemetry (athletic combine measures, or multi-source fantasy projections) must be rescaled to a common dimensionless scale before weighting, exactly the SPARQ pattern. In GSE this is the odds-free projection-fusion index; in GSI it is the commensurable athleticism / load index. The opacity veto travels with it: a composite whose weights and normalization are unpublished is unauditable and should be replaced by its component columns.
layer2.telemetry: Per-component raw value and percentile, the peer reference group, weight vector w_i, composite distribution, and correlation of the composite with the target outcome. The 'correct' weights are LATENT_UNIDENTIFIABLE without a published, validated specification.

reasoning_traces.think: This book is a ladder from a pile of raw facts to a model, and the sovereign reading is that every rung adds an assumption that can break. The author opens by calling raw data 'the numerical equivalent of a pile of footballs' — more than the brain can hold — and defines analysis as compressing that pile into something that fits in your head. That compression is never free. The first rung is the summary statistic, and the book immediately flags that some summaries (QBR, WORP) are opaque while others (yards per catch) are transparent, invoking Moneyball's lesson that batting average hid what on-base percentage revealed. The second rung is the model, and here the book prints real equations rather than hand-waving. Start with ordinary least squares. The linear form y = b0 + b1*x1 + ... + bn*xn is fit by choosing coefficients that minimize the total sum of squared residuals; the footnote explains that squaring keeps residuals positive so the model cannot cheat by underpredicting everything into negative numbers. That is a genuine, dimensionally clean objective, not a toy heuristic. But the book's own touchdown fit exposes the first breakdown: it is a linear probability model, and for mid-field yardlines it returns negative probabilities. A probability cannot be negative, so the linear output map is inadmissible for a chance. The fix is the logistic link, 1/(1+exp(-(b0+...+bn*xn))), which maps the real line into (0,1) by construction. This is the cleanest example in the corpus of a breakdown regime driving a kernel choice: the symptom (negative probabilities) is not patched by clipping but by changing the output map to one whose range is the probability simplex. The same right-hand-side tricks — squares, logs, interactions, fixed effects — survive the switch, because the link only changes how the linear predictor becomes an output. The third rung is interpretation, and the book's best teaching moment is holding things constant. The first_down coefficient on win probability added starts at 0.0573, but first-down plays also gain more yards (15 versus under 4), so part of that coefficient is really the yards, not the new set of downs. Add yards_gained to the model and the first_down coefficient falls to 0.0224 — less than half. That drop is omitted-variable bias made visible, and it is the operational meaning of a partial effect: the coefficient is what remains of a variable's association once the other included variables are held fixed. The crucial caveat, which the book states, is that 'held constant' is a claim about the model's conditioning set, not a certificate of causation; if a confounder is missing, or a control is itself an outcome, the partial effect is still biased. The fourth rung is the composite score, and the book is refreshingly hostile to it. SPARQ and passer rating combine weighting with rescaling: raw components in incompatible units (forty time in seconds, vertical in inches) are first converted to percentiles against a peer group, then weighted into one number. The rescaling is what makes the sum dimensionally legitimate; without it you would be adding seconds to inches. But the author refuses to trust composites because their weights and normalizations are unpublished — 'do you know how to calculate QBR?' — and prefers the component columns. That opacity veto is the through-line of the whole book: a compression you cannot audit is a compression you cannot trust. Read sovereignly, the ladder teaches that each step from data to insight buys convenience with an assumption, and the discipline is to name the assumption, watch for its breakdown symptom, and keep the auditable components rather than the opaque index.
reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: The hidden state of this book was created by a specific scar: the gap between a true relationship and the noisy one we measure. The author stages it with a fair coin — calling heads cannot affect the toss, that is the true relationship, yet a hundred random flips will still show some apparent effect. That separation of true from observed is the wound the entire significance chapter tries to heal. The lineage runs from 'math class' y=mx+b through statsmodels OLS to the replicability crisis, and the book's own origin story is humbler still: the author learned Python, Pandas, and SQL to build fantasymath.com and beat his friends at fantasy football. The data descends from nflfastR, written by Sebastian Carl and Ben Baldwin. So the cognitive source code here is not abstract statistics but a practitioner's hard-won suspicion of any number that looks cleaner than the noisy reality that produced it.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: Model the agents around a fantasy decision under pressure. The author predicts the fantasy market is efficient — he guesses any coefficient on, say, ending last season on IR would be insignificant once ADP is controlled — so he expects the crowd to have already priced the obvious. The league-mate who drafts on gut believes the crowd overreacts to injury news and expects to find value the models miss. Recurse: the author knows the gut drafter thinks the market overreacts, so he expects that drafter to reach for 'bounce-back' players; the gut drafter knows the author trusts the efficient-market coefficient, so he expects to be told his pick is already priced. Meanwhile the defensive coordinator sets a tendency trap that the quarterback's internal clock, decaying under pressure, misreads as open coverage. Each agent is modelling the others' calibration errors, and the only stable arbiter is the held-out result, not anyone's confidence.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: Let the layers veto in order. A linear probability model proposes a mid-field touchdown probability of negative 0.005; the probability layer vetoes it outright and demands the logistic link, because a chance cannot be negative. A first_down coefficient of 0.0573 proposes a large new-set-of-downs effect; the holding-constant layer vetoes the uncontrolled number and re-estimates with yards_gained, dropping it to 0.0224, because part of the effect was confounded yards. An opaque composite proposes a single quarterback rating; the auditability layer vetoes it and demands the component columns, because unpublished weights cannot be checked. And any fusion that smuggles sportsbook odds into its inputs is vetoed by doctrine before any of this runs. A call survives only if its output map is admissible, its controls block the confounders, and its weights are auditable.

reasoning_traces.think: The second pass reads the book as an epistemic discipline rather than a coding manual, and its center of gravity is the significance chapter. The author defines a p-value operationally: assume the true effect is none, then ask how often data this extreme would appear under that assumption. The coin-flip regression makes it concrete — guessing tails appeared to lower the call-success probability by almost 0.13, a huge effect if true, but P>|t| was about 0.21, meaning a draw that extreme happens roughly a fifth of the time under the null. So the effect is noise. The traditional 0.05 threshold is then exposed as fragile: a hundred researchers testing relationships that do not exist will produce about five 'significant' results purely by chance, and those five get published. Worse, a single analyst can run enough variations — adding a variable here, changing a data assumption there — to manufacture significance, and then the traditional interpretation of the p-value 'goes out the window'. The book names this the replicability crisis and prescribes pre-registration (write the regression before running it and stick to it) and stricter thresholds. This is exactly the Foundry's held-out discipline expressed in statistics. Scoring a fit on the same rows used to search for it is the p-hacking sin; pre-registration is the protocol that separates the search set from the evaluation set. The sovereign move is to treat every claimed edge as a null-survival frequency that must be re-tested on independent data, and to count how many specifications were tried, because the family-wise error rate, not the nominal p-value, governs whether the edge is real. The book even insists that an insignificant effect can still be interesting, which guards against the opposite failure of dismissing a true but underpowered signal. The surrounding chapters reinforce the same discipline from the engineering side. Gall's Law — a complex system that works invariably evolved from a simple system that worked — is the methodological commitment to start with a working baseline and grow it, which mirrors extracting a clean linear kernel before adding nonlinear links. 'Get quick feedback' and DRY are the tight-loop verification habits that catch errors as they happen rather than after a giant untested build. The win_prob function example, which takes score, possession, and time left and returns each team's chance of winning, is the exact shape of the Coach-Mind simulator's bounded probability kernel, and it is no accident that it appears as the book's illustration of why functions let you think less: the probability calculation is encapsulated so it can be reused and audited in one place. The state-dependence kernels close the loop. The quadratic marginal effect b1 + 2*b2*x says the value of an extra unit of ADP depends on where you are in the draft, and the turnover-by-fourth-quarter interaction says a turnover costs about 0.12 in win probability normally but 0.20 late — the effect of an event depends on the state in which it occurs. Both are the football-specific face of a general truth the 22-player system lives by: transition costs and marginal values are state-dependent, not constant. Read together with the significance discipline, the book's durable artifact is a single rule: build the simplest admissible kernel, let its breakdown symptoms drive the next refinement, keep every weight and control auditable, and never believe an edge that was found by searching until it survives an independent hold-out. Nothing here invents a football-era origin for pure math; the calculus and the logistic link are standard, and the football content is the observation and decision context the book actually documents.
reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: The significance chapter carries the deepest scar in the book, and it is a field-level wound rather than a personal one. The replicability crisis arose because publication incentives rewarded interesting, significant results, so the lucky five percent of null findings got printed while the honest nulls sat in drawers; the p-value's nominal meaning silently expired once researchers could search many specifications. The author's remedy — pre-registration, stricter thresholds, accepting interesting nulls — is the sediment of that crisis. Gall's Law carries a softer scar: every programmer who tried to write a complex system from scratch and failed learned that working complexity must evolve from working simplicity. Reading these as scars rather than tips is what turns a coding tutorial into a discipline of verified, auditable, held-out knowledge.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: Recurse the beliefs of the people who run and read regressions. The researcher wants a significant result because it publishes; the reviewer suspects the researcher tried many specifications; the researcher knows the reviewer suspects this, so he pre-registers to buy credibility; the reviewer, anticipating that pre-registration can itself be gamed, discounts the headline and looks at the hold-out. The author models the fantasy crowd as efficient and expects no systematic mispricing, while the gut drafter models the crowd as overreactive and expects to exploit it; each is modelling the other's calibration error. The defensive coordinator models the quarterback as a decaying internal clock and sets a trap that looks like open coverage; the quarterback models the coordinator as blitz-prone and speeds up, which is the misread the trap wants. The only belief that survives all this recursion is the one checked on independent data.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: Adjudicate a high-EV call against the layers. Suppose a searched regression reports a 'significant' edge worth drafting on; the multiple-comparisons layer vetoes it because the analyst tried many specifications and the nominal p-value no longer controls the family-wise error, so the edge must survive a pre-registered hold-out first. Suppose a turnover-cost model uses the constant 0.12 in a late-game situation; the state-dependence layer vetoes it and applies the interaction, raising the cost to 0.20, because the effect of a turnover depends on the quarter. Suppose a composite index ranks a prospect; the auditability layer vetoes the opaque index and demands the percentile components and published weights. And doctrine vetoes any input that is a sportsbook odds line. A call is admissible only after it survives the hold-out, the state-dependence correction, the auditability check, and the odds-free rule.

universal_lens: A polymath audit lens for any data-to-model ladder: every compression from raw facts to a single number buys convenience with an assumption, so name the assumption at each rung and watch for its breakdown symptom. A linear probability map breaks when it returns negative chances; a coefficient breaks when a confounder is omitted; a composite breaks when its weights are unpublished; a significance claim breaks under specification search. Keep the auditable components, prefer the simplest admissible kernel, and trust only what survives an independent hold-out.
gsi_mapping: Map the rescaling-and-weighting kernel onto GSI composite telemetry: heterogeneous athletic and clinical measures (forty time, shuttle, vertical jump, load counts) must be percentile-rescaled against a peer group before weighting into a commensurable risk or athleticism index, exactly the SPARQ pattern. The holding-constant operator isolates a biomarker's partial effect controlling for confounders; the logistic link bounds an injury-risk probability to (0,1); and the replicability crisis is the clinical false-positive biomarker warning that demands pre-registered, held-out validation before any index drives a decision.
gse_mapping: Map OLS and the logistic link to the Coach-Mind play-outcome and win-probability kernels (the book's own win_prob function is the template), with the linear probability model vetoed whenever it returns negative chances. Holding-constant disentangles play-type effects (first down versus yards gained); the turnover-by-fourth-quarter interaction encodes state-dependent deception and pressure cost; the quadratic marginal effect captures diminishing draft value. The p-value/pre-registration discipline is the falsifier-led, held-out edge-hunt protocol, and composite fusion is the odds-free DFS portfolio index with auditable weights.
